To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined two structures of the KATP channel in the presence of ATP and ADP and Mg2+, and that the nucleotide binding domains of SUR1 dimerize in both structures.
the molecular structure of human K(ATP) channels in complex with ATP, ADP, and Mg2+ was determined by cryo-EM.

we solved the molecular structure of human K+ATP channels in complex with ATP/ADP at 3.5-5.6 Å resolution, and found a regulatory element in the structure that explains the ability of ADP to override ATP inhibition of channel activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, regulation, and function of ATP-dependent K+ channels (KATP channels) in pancreatic beta cells and in the brain.
the molecular mechanism by which KATP channels are regulated by intracellular ATP and ADP in pancreatic beta cells.
the molecular mechanism of the KATP channels, a family of ion channels that are important for the regulation of cellular excitability and insulin secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KATP channel is a dimer, with two SUR1 subunits and two Kir6.2 subunits.
the KATP channel is a heterooctameric complex composed of four SUR1 and four Kir6.2 subunits, with the SUR1 subunits arranged in a head-to-head configuration.
SUR1 acts as an ADP-sensor, overriding the ATP-inhibition of the KATP-channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KATP channels are regulated by the intracellular nucleotides ATP and ADP, which are the products of the metabolic pathway.
ADP is a potent activator of KATP, and that ATP inhibition of KATP can be overcome by the presence of ADP.
the structure of the KATP channel is a complex of the SUR1 ABC transporter with the Kir6.2 K+ channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lasso extension is a key regulatory element for ADP’s ability of override ATP inhibition.
the lasso is the critical regulatory element in ADPs activation of KATP.
the lasso extension is a key regulatory element for ADP’s ability in KATP channel to override ATP inhibition.
